Where to record a deed

Anything affecting title to Horry County land, whether a deed, a mortgage or a plat, is filed at the Register of Deeds, 1301 Second Avenue, Conway, SC 29526. Weekday hours are 8:00 AM to 4:45 PM. The Customer Service and Recording Desk shuts early on the final day of the fiscal year, so phone ahead if you plan a June 30 visit.

The office also offers e-recording, a Request for Documents form, escrow accounts, and a Recording Notification Service that alerts you to fraudulent filings against your property. Details are at horrycountysc.gov.

Recording fees and the state deed fee

Two separate charges usually apply. The first is the office's own recording fee, a flat sum per document ever since per-page pricing ended on August 1, 2019. The office page links a PDF price list, so read it or call before closing. The second is the deed fee, often called doc stamps, collected for the state and county.

Title 12, Chapter 24 sets the deed fee at $1.85 for each $500 of value, counting any partial $500. Of each $1.85, $1.30 is the state's share and $0.55 goes into the county general fund. What you pay tracks the value written in the deed.

  • "Value" covers anything paid or owed for the property, whether cash or something of equal worth.
  • A loan that stays in place both before and after the transfer can come off the value.
  • The grantor (seller) is the main party liable, with the grantee (buyer) liable second.
  • Someone tied to the deal signs a value affidavit that travels with the deed.

Deeds that are exempt from the deed fee

The long list in Section 12-24-40 excuses certain transfers from the fee, yet the deed must still carry an affidavit naming the exemption. The ones sellers see most are:

  • Transfers where the property is worth $100 or less.
  • Transfers to a federal, state or local government body, including a school district.
  • A deed that returns property to a mortgage holder by foreclosure or deed in lieu.
  • A corrective or quitclaim deed that only confirms title already held, with no payment.
  • Transfers between family partnerships or family trusts, or to a partner or beneficiary, with no payment.
  • Transfers with no recognized gain or loss under Internal Revenue Code Section 1041.

If your situation is not a clean match, treat the fee as owed and ask the register of deeds what it will take.

Why a deed gets rejected

One firm rule applies to time-shares: a vacation time-sharing deed must carry a clear notice on its first page and be titled "Vacation Time Sharing Ownership Deed," or the office will not accept it. Owners of a time-share interest should keep that in mind.

Before you submit, run through this list:

  • Names, legal description and tax map number match the prior recorded deed.
  • The value affidavit or exemption statement is signed.
  • The fee enclosed matches the current schedule.
  • Mail goes to the P.O. Box, and in-person delivery goes to the Second Avenue address.

If anything is unclear, call (843) 915-5430 before an original leaves your hands.

Property tax after a sale

Taxes are billed to the owner of record, which makes the date a deed is recorded important. Real property notices are mailed each October 1, and the balance is due by the following January 15. Late payments pick up penalties on January 16, February 2 and March 17, and a bill that goes missing does not erase them.

Following a sale, the Tax Assessor at (843) 915-5040 is the contact. That office also processes address changes and the owner-occupied residence classification. Passing along an existing interest, a life estate included, is an assessable transfer that brings a new appraisal, and the 15 percent ceiling on increases is set aside for the year the transfer first shows up on a bill.

  • Tax Assessor, (843) 915-5040: sold property, address changes, residence and farm classification.
  • Auditor, (843) 915-5051: homestead exemption.
  • Treasurer, (843) 428-2126: payments by mail, in person or by phone.

Values are revisited every fifth year. Legal residence property is taxed at 4 percent of value, and the application is due before the first penalty date, which means a buyer who moves in files separately from you.

Horry County at a glance

By land area, 1,133.31 square miles, no other South Carolina county is bigger, and only three have more people. Horry counted 351,029 residents in 2020 and is estimated at 427,551 for 2025, with retirees and second-home buyers behind most of the growth.

Myrtle Beach is the biggest community, and Conway is the seat. Plenty of owners live somewhere else, and a family-owned house may still be titled in an older relative's name. Straightening out the chain of title at the register of deeds usually comes before anything else in a sale.

Selling with title or tax problems

Look up your recorded deed in the online index first, and see whether the name there is the name of the person selling. When an heir inherited the house and no estate was ever opened, expect the title company to ask for that paperwork before closing.

The tax account comes next. Anything left unpaid past the March 17 penalty date remains on the account, so get a payoff figure from the Treasurer before choosing a closing date.

Cash Home Buyers can look at a Horry County house as it stands, including one with an unrecorded deed, back taxes or a tenant, and explain the steps in writing.

A sensible order is to verify the deed name, record whatever documents are missing, obtain the payoff and only then book the closing. The title company files the new deed and sends the county its money out of the proceeds. The deed fee usually falls on the seller, so read the settlement sheet ahead of time and you will know the number.

Keep a copy of the recorded deed and the closing statement. If a question about the tax account arises later, the recording date and the names on the deed are the first things any county office will ask for.

A short list for the day of closing: a photo ID, the payoff letter if you requested one, and any estate or trust documents tied to the property. The title company handles the filing itself, so you do not need to go to Conway unless you are recording a document on your own.

Frequently asked questions

How much does the Horry County Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?

Recording uses flat per-document fees that took effect August 1, 2019, listed in a price PDF on the office page. The state deed fee is separate, at $1.85 per $500 of value.

Who pays the deed fee when selling a house in Horry County?

The seller is generally liable under state law and the buyer is second in line. Who really pays shows up in your contract and on the settlement sheet.

Can I record a deed in Horry County by mail?

Yes, send it to P.O. Box 470, Conway, SC 29528, or bring it to 1301 Second Avenue. A quick phone call first will confirm the fees and what else is required.

Does a foreclosure or deed in lieu pay the deed fee?

No. A transfer of mortgaged property to the mortgage holder through foreclosure or deed in lieu is exempt, though the deed still needs an affidavit stating the reason.

Who should I call about taxes after selling my Horry County house?

Call the Tax Assessor, (843) 915-5040, about a sold property and the Treasurer, (843) 428-2126, about a bill. Tax follows the owner of record, so get the deed recorded quickly.
